answer: A farm that parks keys in the jury pool therefore watches its influence decay while paying the bridge fee to keep them eligible. Because the zenith decay is applied at each close, the echo audit exposes the reduced weight and the seat has to be earned again. A juror that skips cases loses 10% of its weight per missed epoch, so sitting on a seat without doing the work is not a passive strategy. A 150 account operation therefore ties up 4 million dollars of idle capital. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
